$comment: Per-muscle dose ranges and dose notes removed from assets/data/muscles.json on 2026-09-02.
Withdrawn on the owner's decision after the reflexpmr audit found the 'Botox' column tracked the Xeomin label.
Kept here for provenance only. Not loaded by the app. Do not restore without re-verifying every value against current labeling.

2026-09-03: 29 dose figures that lived in PROSE (pearls, placement, setup, safetyNotes) removed as well - see `prose`. This is the class a field-level withdrawal misses (reflexpmr RETURN-HANDOFF s.1); reflexpmr strips such items at import. 11 items shared with the reflexpmr import were dropped whole to match it; 18 in muscles reflexpmr never imported had only the figure removed, the rest of the sentence kept verbatim. Originals are recorded here so any can be restored after re-verification against current labeling.

pec-major.dosageNote: Total across both heads. Split dose between clavicular and sternal heads (e.g. 25-50U each).

lat-dorsi.dosageNote: Large muscle — distribute across 2-3 sites along the posterior axillary fold.

subscapularis.dosageNote: Distribute across multiple sites along the muscle belly. Deep injection — confirm tip placement before each.

biceps-brachii.dosageNote: Large muscle with 2 heads. Split across short and long heads. FDA PI allows up to 200 U.

brachialis.dosageNote: Deep to biceps — often underdosed. Confirm placement on US before injecting.

triceps.dosageNote: Rarely injected for spasticity. Confirm genuine spasticity before treating.

brachioradialis.dosageNote: Superficial forearm muscle. Stay lateral and superficial to avoid radial nerve.

pronator-teres.dosageNote: Compact muscle. 1-2 sites in proximal belly.

fcu.dosageNote: Inject proximal third only — ulnar nerve becomes superficial distally.

fds.dosageNote: Dose per head if targeting individual fingers.

fdp.dosageNote: Deep muscle — confirm placement on US.

fpl.dosageNote: Narrow therapeutic window — over-dosing weakens pinch grip. Start low.

ecrl.dosageNote: Draft entry — extensor data added for completeness (dystonia / mixed patterns). Verify every dose, US note, and hazard against current labeling and a primary source before clinical use.

ecrb.dosageNote: Draft entry — extensor data added for completeness (dystonia / mixed patterns). Verify every dose, US note, and hazard against current labeling and a primary source before clinical use.

ecu.dosageNote: Draft entry — extensor data added for completeness (dystonia / mixed patterns). Verify every dose, US note, and hazard against current labeling and a primary source before clinical use.

edc.dosageNote: Draft entry — extensor data added for completeness (dystonia / mixed patterns). Verify every dose, US note, and hazard against current labeling and a primary source before clinical use.

adductor-pollicis.dosageNote: Very small muscle — low doses only. Dorsal approach preferred.

hand-lumbricals.dosageNote: Per individual lumbrical. Very small muscles — start at the low end. Total hand lumbrical dose typically 10-25 U Botox across affected digits.

paraspinals.dosageNote: Dose is per spinal level. Typically inject 2-3 levels per session for a total of 100-300 U Botox. Use conservative initial dosing to avoid excessive trunk extensor weakness.

quadratus-lumborum.dosageNote: Deep muscle requiring curvilinear probe. Distribute across 2-3 sites.

rectus-abdominis.dosageNote: Total across all sites bilaterally. Use conservative dosing — respiratory compromise is a risk with excessive abdominal wall weakness.

obliques.dosageNote: Dose is per side. Combines external and internal oblique as a single injection target. Inject bilaterally only if clinically indicated — monitor for trunk weakness.

gluteus-maximus.dosageNote: One of the largest muscles in the body — distribute across 3-4 sites.

pectineus.dosageNote: Draft entry — added for completeness; doses are illustrative starting references. Verify every dose, ultrasound note, and hazard against current labeling and a primary source before clinical use.

adductor-brevis.dosageNote: Often co-injected with adductor longus and magnus for refractory scissoring.

gracilis.dosageNote: Thin muscle — conservative dosing to avoid spread to adjacent adductors.

rectus-femoris.dosageNote: Primary stiff-knee gait target. 1-2 sites in proximal-mid muscle belly.

vastus-medialis.dosageNote: Use cautiously — weakening VMO can destabilize the patella.

fdb.dosageNote: Plantar injection — painful. Consider topical anesthetic.

add-hallucis.dosageNote: Very small intrinsic foot muscle. Low doses only.

foot-lumbricals.dosageNote: Per individual lumbrical. Tiny muscles — start low. Usually only inject the clinically affected digits, not all four.

splenius-cervicis.dosageNote: Draft entry — added for completeness; doses are illustrative starting references. Verify every dose, ultrasound note, and hazard against current labeling and a primary source before clinical use.

obliquus-capitis-inferior.dosageNote: Draft entry — added for completeness; doses are illustrative starting references. Verify every dose, ultrasound note, and hazard against current labeling and a primary source before clinical use. Vertebral artery is immediately deep — image guidance mandatory.

frontalis.dosageNote: Total across all forehead sites (4-5 sites at 2-5 U each). For brow dystonia, use the minimum effective dose. For cosmetic treatment, 10-20 U total is standard. This is NOT a typical spasticity target.

corrugator-supercilii.dosageNote: Per side. Per the Allergan PI for blepharospasm, inject 5 U at each corrugator site. For cosmetic use (glabellar lines), the standard FDA-approved dose is 4 U Botox per corrugator (bilateral total 20 U including procerus).

procerus.dosageNote: Single midline injection. Per the Allergan PI for blepharospasm, 5 U at the procerus is standard. For cosmetic use (glabellar lines), 4 U Botox at the procerus is standard (part of the 20 U glabellar complex with corrugators).

orbicularis-oculi.dosageNote: Shown as total per eye. Deliver as 1.25-2.5 U per site across 6 sites per eye (total 7.5-15 U Botox per eye; bilateral 15-30 U). Per the Allergan PI for blepharospasm, the initial recommended dose is 1.25-2.5 U per site; do not exceed 5 U per site or 200 U total over 30 days.

temporalis.dosageNote: Per side. Distribute across 2-3 sites within the temporal fossa. Prioritize the anterior fibers for jaw-closing dystonia.

masseter.dosageNote: Per side. For bilateral bruxism, inject both sides. Reduce dose in smaller or elderly patients. Total bilateral session dose 50-100 U Botox.

lateral-pterygoid.dosageNote: Per side. Lower doses are used due to the small muscle volume and proximity to the medial pterygoid. Always use EMG guidance.

medial-pterygoid.dosageNote: Per side. The medial pterygoid is smaller than the masseter — use lower doses. Consider co-injection with the masseter for refractory jaw-closing dystonia.

mentalis.dosageNote: Per side. Bilateral total: 5-10 U Botox. Start at the lower end of the dosing range to minimize risk of oral incompetence. The mentalis is a small muscle — small doses are effective.

platysma.dosageNote: Total dose across all sites per side. For anterocollis, 25-50 U Botox per side distributed across 2-4 platysmal bands. For cosmetic neck banding, 2-5 U per site along each band (lower total dose). Use the minimum effective dose to avoid dysphagia.

prose.original: Use 25-50U Botox per injection site, distributed across 2-3 sites per head, for a total session dose as listed in the dosage field.
Very low doses are appropriate given the small muscle volume — start at 10-20 U Botox per site.
Low doses only (10-25 U Botox) given the small muscle volume
Very small — use hockey-stick probe and minimal doses (10-20U Botox)
Tiny muscles requiring tiny doses — 5-10 U Botox per lumbrical is usually sufficient; overdosing weakens grip
Small muscle — conservative dosing (25-50U Botox per muscle)
Thin muscle — easy to over-inject. Start with very low doses (10-25U Botox)
Start with low doses (15-25 U Botox per muscle) and titrate up — overcorrection or nerve spread can be disabling
Often the highest-dose muscle in cervical dystonia treatment — 50-100 U Botox per side

Excessive dosing or bilateral injection can cause severe neck extensor weakness and anterocollis (dropped head syndrome) — use the minimum effective dose (25-50 U Botox per side) and monitor for neck weakness at follow-up.
Use conservative doses (25-50 U per side) — excessive weakening causes dropped head syndrome (anterocollis)
Inject at 2-3 vertebral levels per session; dose listed is per level — total session dose may be 100-300 U Botox across all levels
prose.replacement: Inject at 2-3 vertebral levels per session.

prose.original: Aspirate before injecting. Distribute the total dose across 2-4 sites (25-50 U Botox per site).
prose.replacement: Aspirate before injecting. Distribute the total dose across 2-4 sites.

prose.original: Start with conservative doses (50 U Botox total) — excessive weakening can impair cough and respiratory function
prose.replacement: Excessive weakening can impair cough and respiratory function

prose.original: Small muscle — use conservative doses (25-50U Botox)
Low doses only — 10-25U Botox typically sufficient
Extremely small muscles — 5-10 U Botox per lumbrical is typical; most patients need only 1-2 lumbricals treated
prose.replacement: Extremely small muscles — most patients need only 1-2 lumbricals treated

prose.original: Excessive dosing risks weakening adjacent deep extensors (semispinalis capitis, multifidus) due to toxin spread, potentially causing or worsening anterocollis — use the minimum effective dose (25-50 U Botox per side).
prose.replacement: Excessive dosing risks weakening adjacent deep extensors (semispinalis capitis, multifidus) due to toxin spread, potentially causing or worsening anterocollis — use the minimum effective dose.

prose.original: Conservative dosing (25-50 U per side) — toxin spread to adjacent deep extensors can cause dropped head
prose.replacement: Conservative dosing — toxin spread to adjacent deep extensors can cause dropped head

prose.original: Inject 2-5 U Botox per site. The total dose is typically 10-20 U distributed across all sites.
NOT a spasticity target — it is injected for cosmetic forehead lines, rare brow dystonia, or as part of migraine PREEMPT protocol (20 U total, 5 U per site x 4 sites)
prose.replacement: NOT a spasticity target — it is injected for cosmetic forehead lines, rare brow dystonia, or as part of migraine PREEMPT protocol

prose.original: Inject 5-10 U Botox per side (per the Allergan PI). A single site per side is typically sufficient, though some practitioners split across 2 sites for broader coverage.
prose.replacement: A single site per side is typically sufficient, though some practitioners split across 2 sites for broader coverage.

prose.original: Inject 5-10 U Botox as a single midline injection.
Inject 1.25-2.5 U Botox (or equivalent) per site. Use a tuberculin syringe for precise dosing at these low volumes.
prose.replacement: Use a tuberculin syringe for precise dosing at these low volumes.

prose.original: Reconstitute Botox at a concentration that allows injection of small volumes per site (e.g., 2.5 U per 0.1 mL = 100 U / 4 mL dilution, or 5 U per 0.1 mL = 100 U / 2 mL dilution). The Allergan PI recommends 1.25-2.5 U per site.
prose.replacement: Reconstitute at a concentration that allows injection of small volumes per site.

prose.original: In migraine patients, temporalis injection sites overlap with PREEMPT protocol sites — 20 U per side (5 U x 4 sites) per the Allergan PREEMPT paradigm
prose.replacement: In migraine patients, temporalis injection sites overlap with PREEMPT protocol sites

prose.original: Inject 2.5-5 U Botox per side as a single midline injection per side (2 injection sites total for bilateral treatment).
prose.replacement: A single injection per side (2 injection sites total for bilateral treatment).

prose.original: Very low doses are effective for this small muscle — start with 2.5 U Botox per side and titrate up only if needed
prose.replacement: Very low doses are effective for this small muscle — titrate up only if needed

prose.original: For NECK BANDING (cosmetic): Inject along the visible platysmal bands with smaller doses per site (2-5 U Botox per site).
prose.replacement: For NECK BANDING (cosmetic): Inject along the visible platysmal bands with smaller doses per site.
